quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, apply both the front and rear brakes together and shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Help you blend in with traffic.
Give you an escape route.
Allow other riders to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you an escape route.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see other vehicles and be seen. It keeps you away from wind gusts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also prevents other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your chance of a collision?

options.text: Keep enough space between you and other vehicles.
Ride very slowly.
Ride in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space between you and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Always give yourself a safe space cushion around your motorcycle. Keep this space when following vehicles, being followed, passing, being passed, or lane sharing.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: To let other riders know you are near them.
To help other drivers see you in slow traffic.
To warn drivers that you are slowing or stopping in an unexpected place.

questions.correctAnswerText: To warn drivers that you are slowing or stopping in an unexpected place.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light to alert other drivers when you slow down or stop where they may not expect it. This is especially important before making a sharp, fast turn off a highway.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: Only at night.
Only during the day.
During the day and at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the day and at night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright, reflective clothing whenever you ride.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping a motorcycle, what should you do with the gears?

options.text: Do not change gears.
Shift up through the gears.
Shift down through the gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears using the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: What does the Motorcycle Safety Foundation's SEE strategy stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: The SEE strategy helps riders make safe decisions. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Go slowly and be careful.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, stop completely and wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before moving. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: When should you use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch?

options.text: When the throttle is stuck and won't move.
When you start to lose control on a curve.
When the motorcycle starts to wobble.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the throttle is stuck and won't move.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it, press the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch right away. This stops power to the rear wheel so you can safely leave the road.

questions.question: How should your jacket and pants fit while riding?

options.text: Loose enough for wind to catch the fabric.
Snug enough to not flap in the wind.
Tight enough to limit your movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug enough to not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Your jacket and pants should fit snugly so they do not flap, but loose enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to tell the other vehicle to go.
Drive through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can become dirty and block your view.
Mirrors are never reliable.
Motorcycles have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. You need to check more than just your mirrors to stay aware of what is around you.

questions.question: What is the minimum age to get a driver license in South Dakota?

options.text: 14 years old
16 years old
18 years old

questions.correctAnswerText: 14 years old
questions.explanation: In South Dakota, you must be at least 14 years old to get a driver license. You must also meet all other state requirements.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do when other vehicles are slowed or stopped?

options.text: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes of traffic.
It is fine for a motorcyclist to weave in and out of traffic lanes.
A motorcyclist should ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between rows of stopped or slow vehicles is dangerous. Vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to be safe.

questions.question: What should motorcycle passengers do?

options.text: Look over their shoulder when taking a turn or curve.
Never hold onto the rider.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder when taking a turn or curve.
questions.explanation: Before the ride starts, ask your passenger to look over your shoulder in the direction of any turn or curve. This helps you and your motorcycle lean in the right direction.

questions.question: Which one does NOT affect how quickly a person's blood alcohol concentration (BAC) goes up?

options.text: The number of drinks consumed
How fast a person drinks
How often a person drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks
questions.explanation: Factors that affect how quickly your BAC rises include how many drinks you have, how fast you drink, your sex, your weight, and whether you have eaten recently.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get across the surface faster.
Make the weaving worse to get other drivers' attention.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves over grooves or gratings, just keep a steady speed and go straight across. Trying to correct the weave by riding at an angle makes you zigzag, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle gives the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-fourths of a motorcycle's stopping power. Use both the front and rear brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist change gears before starting a turn?

options.text: To prevent a sudden change in power during the turn.
To keep both hands on the handle grips during the turn.
To prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent a sudden change in power during the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. Shifting while turning can cause a sudden power change to the rear wheel and cause a skid. If you must shift during a turn, do it smoothly.

questions.question: In areas where danger might be present, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Keep their speed the same.
Assume they will be safe.
Cover the clutch and both brakes to react faster in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and both brakes to react faster in an emergency.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, schools, or construction zones, slow down. Cover the clutch and both brakes to be ready to react quickly if you need to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the road ahead will be divided.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Usually a good way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Get off the roadway.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle tailgaters is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make things more dangerous.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
Be parked without a wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.
